key_insight: Learning test-time ensemble weights depends on both labeled questions Q and generations N: buffered ERM achieves excess risk Õ(Q^−1/2 + N^−β/2), while a simplified model reveals three minimax regimes.
engineering_relevance: The theory suggests balancing spending on labeled questions and generations, with cross-question pooling potentially improving learning when questions are plentiful.
method: Analyze calibrated margin-buffered ERM under a margin condition with exponent β.
Characterize minimax risk for two models and two answers using a Hellinger modulus.
Use polynomial approximation and spectral analysis to identify three learning regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds, not empirical benchmarks, including an N^−β identification floor in the simplified model even with infinitely many questions.
watch_item: The guarantees target infinite-generation voting risk; matching pooled estimators for general ensembles and precise regime transitions remain open.
paper_title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory
